final_note: You worked through the key terms in Materials.

concepts.def: ρ = m/V, mass per unit volume of a substance, measured in kg m⁻³.
F = kx for an elastic material below the limit of proportionality.
E = stress/strain, a measure of stiffness, measured in pascals.
σ = F/A, force per unit cross-sectional area, in pascals.
ε = ΔL/L, fractional change in length; dimensionless.
Maximum stress beyond which a material does not return to its original length when load is removed.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Materials — a core area of A-Level Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Materials brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Materials.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
